title: Scalars and Custom Types
description: Use built-in scalars and create custom scalar types.

data.text: Scalars are the leaf nodes of your schema — they represent raw values like integers, strings, and booleans. Hot Chocolate supports many built-in scalars and lets you create custom ones.
Hot Chocolate provides additional scalars out of the box, including `Date`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`, `Uri`, and `Guid`.

data.title: Using Extended Scalars

data.text: When built-in scalars aren't enough, create a custom scalar by implementing `ISerializationTypeDefinition` or using the simpler `[GraphQLType]` approach.

data.title: Custom Email Scalar
data.content: Create a reusable email scalar that validates format.

data.title: Reuse Custom Scalars
data.text: Package custom scalars as a shared library so they can be reused across multiple GraphQL services in your organization.

terms.definition: A primitive type like Int, String, or Boolean that represents a single value.
A user-defined scalar that adds validation or serialization logic.
Hot Chocolate interface for defining how a custom scalar serializes and parses values.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GraphQL has built-in scalars for common types
Hot Chocolate adds Date, DateTime, and more
Custom scalars let you enforce validation rules
Register custom types in DI during startup
data.takeaway: Next, we'll build queries and mutations with these types.
